ferry.nombre: Part 4 · The Last Ferry: Passenger Cabin and Aft Deck
ferry.nota:
**A4-E03, aboard.** The last ferry to Bainbridge: a 35-minute crossing, some **forty passengers**, all mortal, six crew, and **security cameras in the cabin** (three “CCTV” objects on the map; they aren't ANOMALY). This map is the **passenger deck** (the boat's second level), cropped to the stern: the cabin continues forward (hatched strip) and isn't played.

**Pell** “is in the second-floor passenger cabin, by a window, with the briefcase handcuffed to his wrist” (Wits + Investigation Diff. 3 to find him): put him in the marked **port booth**, by the window, with Dawson and the ghouls nearby. If they voted with the coterie, **Fry** is in another booth with headphones on (“The last boat of the night. I told you.”). In the cabin, forty witnesses: any visible supernatural act is **Thermometer +2**. Presence (Daunt) to keep the passengers in the cabin: Charisma + Intimidation Diff. 3. Potence to break the briefcase cuff without taking off Pell's hand: Strength + Larceny Diff. 3.

**Aft outer deck.** When the ferry casts off, the gangway pulls back: the **gate** in the rail stays shut and the “Down the ramp” region only works while docked (disable it on departure, at 12:55 a.m.). This is where the negotiation with Halloway happens if he's aboard (“He offers everything: money, domain, the Sheriff's post”). **Jumping into the water from the stern: 6 meters**; the water is in the high forties and the current is strong: Stamina + Athletics Diff. 3 to reach shore or Salt's launch, which follows the ferry and can board over the stern. Jump with the briefcase and the drive is lost. Throwing the briefcase overboard is the fastest way to destroy it.

**Transitions.** The starboard and port stairs (by the aft end of the cabin) go down to the **car deck** (`ferry-coches`). The **bridge stair**, in the middle of the cabin, goes up to the upper deck and the **bridge** (`ferry-puente`): that's where Halloway runs (“uses Daunt and flees toward the bridge to take control of the ship”).

**Galley** in the middle of the cabin (fixed counters). The booth benches and tables are bolted to the floor (they're fixed; there's no movable furniture on this map).

ferry-coches.nombre: Part 4 · The Last Ferry: Car Deck
ferry-coches.nota:
**A4-E03, the car deck.** “On the car deck, among the vehicles, there are few witnesses: normal Masquerade Difficulty.” It's the best place to fight: Dawson and the ghouls fight to protect the briefcase. **Krell**, if he survived and reached 3 steps in A3-E03, “shows up on the car deck to help David”; if not, he shows up to recover the folios, as a third force.

Crop: the aft ~22 m of the deck (the rest of the boat continues forward: the strip along the west edge, behind a chain, isn't played). Along the sides, the **casings** (ventilation and machinery: you see their sheet-metal tops with the grilles; not played) with the starboard and port **stairs** up to the cabin (`ferry`). The **cars** are movable tiles (thirteen, in five lanes): they can be pushed, used as cover, and have their windows smashed; the Storyteller moves them or removes them.

**The open stern.** The deck ends at the **stern chain**; the center section unhooks when docking, and that's where the terminal's **vehicle ramp** comes in (the “Down the vehicle ramp” region, docked only: disable it on departure). Anyone who arrives late by car and reaches the ferry before it casts off comes in here. Jumping into the water from the open stern is a shorter drop than from the passenger deck (about 2 m), with the same swimming roll.

ferry-puente.nombre: Part 4 · The Last Ferry: The Bridge
ferry-puente.nota:
**The bridge.** Halloway “doesn't fight: he uses Daunt and flees toward the bridge to take control of the ship.” He climbs the stair in the middle of the cabin to the **upper deck** and enters the **bridge** (wheelhouse) through the aft door; the crew can lock it from inside. Inside are the captain and a deckhand (two of the six crew): Dominate on them, or Halloway forces them (“Stop.” “Let go of that.”). The **helm station** is in the center, facing the **console** under the forward windows. The starboard and port **bridge wings** (open, with rails) each have a control pedestal.

At night the bridge runs **dark** (only the screens, turned all the way down, to protect night vision): high darkness on purpose. The navigation lights are on the wing rails: green to starboard (north), red to port (south). The two deck lights hang from the wheelhouse's aft bulkhead and light the upper deck; a little of that light gets in through the bridge's aft windows.

Crop: the ferry has two bridges, one at each end; this is the forward one during the crossing (the one steering). Between the cabin stair and the bridge there's more ship that isn't played; the upper deck continues aft (hatched strip). If Halloway falls into the coterie's hands, see Endings (AVE-01-FIN).
